ANDY KAWA VS SAPS STANDOFF

By: Ntokozo Miya | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An opportunistic attack so savage and ruthless, it should have broken her but an Eastern Cape survivor opens up about tracking down the perpetrators, and her twelve-year long fight for justice.

Unique Selling Point:
Andy Kawa takes us behind-the-scenes of her victory against the police ministry – an emotional rollercoaster out of which she came out tops... but did she really? She also details her ongoing battle with depression.

Summary:
In the first week of Dec in 2010, Andy was on top of the world. Her daughter had just completed a Master's in Law at Oxford in the UK and planned to return to SA on the 10th of Dec.

Andy lives in Jhb but was born in the Eastern Cape. In the days leading up to her daughter's return, Andy visited her family in PE. Andy had bought a house for her mother! On the 9th of Dec shortly after lunch, Andy had gone to the property agent's office to sign documents so that the agent would deliver the house keys to Andy's mother the following day.

Andy's flight back to Johannesburg was due for take-off at 5pm. So she decided to take a walk on the beach to pass the time until her flight. She was overwhelmed with pride and excitement, but her light would be dimmed in the worst possible way on the 9th.

While on the beach, she was kidnapped by vagrants and held at knifepoint in a bush near the beachfront. Andy was gang-raped until the early hours of the next morning.

Family and friends notified police but the police search was not thorough. Police did not check the most obvious location where she was held. Andy's horror was extended and her rape ordeal continued for hours longer than it would have been had the police simply done their job with a sense of urgency.

Following the bungled search, the police investigation was also flawed and disregarded leads that could have led to the arrest and capture of her attackers.

Andy then took the SAPS and police minister to court over their failure to find her timeously and investigate her case properly. She won the case and the police were found to have been negligent.

Upon appeal however, the SAPS won and it was determined that they had done everything they can. Dissatisfied, Andy fought on and took the matter to the Constitutional Court. On the 5th of April this year, the Constitutional Court ruled in Andy's favour.

Further information:
Additional speakers provide a supportive narrative to the main account from Andy. They share their impressions of police conduct, their efforts to assist Andy's investigation into her own case and how she has battled not only the police ministry for the past 12 years, but also, frequent and intense bouts of depression.

We visually support the narrative with symbolic, emotive shots of the beach location in Port Elizabeth.

Extra Budget Items:
Clayton, the PE-based cameraman, will be sending me a quote for someone he trusts with security. He will be shooting on the beach where vagrants still live and he'll be doing so in the late afternoon/evening and again early in the morning. I have safety concerns and would prefer that we do not take any chances. I will send quote through ASAP after I get it from him.

Script:


FINAL ANDY KAWA SCRIPT


VO – Gqeberha, one of the Eastern Cape’s most beautiful beachside cities. Attracting both local and international tourists, it’s prized as one of the country’s best surf spots… In December 2010, businesswoman Andy Kawa was spending her last few hours in the city before taking a flight back to Johannesburg…
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
Everytime I’m in PE, I go for a walk on the beach. It's natural for me. I love the sea.
VO - But on that Thursday afternoon, a walk on the beach became a terrifying ordeal.
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
I saw him from afar. And when I looked, something just didn't look right. So I turned to go back. All of a sudden, he held me FROM behind. He told me not to scream, otherwise he would kill me. And he showed me an okapi and a beer bottle.
VO – The knife-wielding man pushed Andy towards the sand dunes, a secluded and bushy area near the shoreline.




ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
His eyes were so vicious that I thought, here is my encounter with the devil.
VO - As evening approached, Andy’s flight left for Jo’burg without her. Unable to reach her by phone, her family grew suspicious.
Immediately, they knew something was wrong, and reported her missing at the city’s Humewood police station.
Next, they set off in search of Andy at Kings Beach, her last known location and just a few minutes from the police station.
VISUALS - Thando drives through in the red car and stops… gets out car… and then...
THANDO RUBUSANA – ANDY'S NEPHEW
This is where she was parked… This is the car she was driving….
VO - Andy’s nephew, Thando Rubusana, found her vandalized car but his aunt was nowhere to be seen. Her family intensified their search, and it was only hours later that the police eventually arrived with a dog unit.
THANDO RUBUSANA – ANDY'S NEPHEW
on that particular day when they were busy searching for her. I [00:07:30.00] think if they just added an additional five minutes of the search time, I think the time that they utilized it was just scrolling through the bushes.
VO - Meanwhile in the nearby sand dunes, Andy’s torment continued throughout the night… blindfolded, naked and with a knife to her neck, she endured a savage sexual assault by multiple men.
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
ANDY - I wasn't aware that there were several. I could see from my linen top that I was blindfolded with. I thought that he was changing pants because I could see different bottoms.
CLAIRE - Is there any particular moment that you recall or you feel for you is probably the lowest moment, the darkest, heaviest moment?
ANDY – As the knife was going down, I saw a picture of my family. They were looking at the coffin that was about to be hoisted down. I'd already resigned that I would die and prayed. And I said, Please, God, may my soul rest in peace.
VO - Hours later, she was freed.
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
It took me a while after he had gone, to feel myself, to see whether I'm safe, to remove the blindfold because I thought it was a trick, that I would move and he would kill me.
VO - Fifteen hours after her nightmare began, Andy was eventually found by a passing jogger who helped her to Humewood police station… But that was NOT the end of her struggle…
VISUALS BREAK, MUSIC
VO - Two years after the crime and frustrated by the lack of progress in her case, Andy launched her own investigation. She began interviewing parking attendants at the beach. With each new lead, she would update the police, but to no avail.
BUSHIE ENGELBRECHT – RETIRED POLICE OFFICER
This case was extremely bungled. I promise you, I couldn't believe all the mistakes they made. It was a comedy of errors from the very outset.
VO - As the investigation dragged on, Andy upped the ante: taking her plight to the High Court. Now retired, Bushie Engelbrecht had spent 43 years in the police. He reviewed Andy's case and what he found was startling…
BUSHIE ENGELBRECHT – RETIRED POLICE OFFICER
The bushes there are very low. So from a helicopter, you will definitely see that. So there wasn't a proper search done in that area. They went in the wrong direction. They said they didn't have enough policemen but Humewood police station was, I think, about two kilometers away with 15 policemen on duty.
THANDO RUBUSANA – ANDY'S NEPHEW
If you can look the distance from where she was walking along the shores to where she was found, you can see that proper job was not being done by the police services
VO – Despite having access to cctv footage on the day of Andy’s attack, it wasn’t collected by the police.
BUSHIE ENGELBRECHT – RETIRED POLICE OFFICER
They saw video footage only five years later. I mean, that is absolutely ridiculous.
VO - Andy argued in the High Court that the inefficient and negligent handling of the investigation had caused her further trauma. She won her case but the police appealed, arguing that their investigation had indeed been thorough. The Supreme Court Justices agreed, overturning the High Court ruling and dealing Andy a significant psychological blow.
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
There was nothing else for me. The only thing I wanted, I wanted some semblance of justice.
VO - The Supreme Court ruling was so devastating that Andy fell into depression. Her daughter, Vee remembers how her mother struggled to cope.
VEE KAWA – ANDY'S DAUGHTER
She was just in her room and in bed. And yeah, I think overcome by not only an overwhelming sense of grief, but at some point it felt like she had lost a sense of who she was.
VO – Battling her mental health, Andy none-the-less decided to fight on, instructing her legal team to approach the Constitutional Court. She again argued the police’s delayed and insufficient search had prolonged her suffering. Moreover, their botched investigation, she said, had caused her “serious psychological and psychiatric trauma”. The Apex Court agreed. Victory.
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
I couldn't even jump and be happy or whatever. I was just stunned. This would be a judgment that would have implications for other victims of crime, who would be able to enforce their right to having criminal cases being investigated was something just powerful.
LINK - So after twelve years, Andy does get a positive result from the Constitutional Court, but is it really a win if the perpetrators have not been caught? Is it really a win if they are going to do it to somebody else?
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
Up to this day, there has not been one person who has been arrested for the case.
VO: Despite repeated attempts to include them in our story, the police ignored our requests for an interview.
VO Meanwhile, Andy has gone from being the person seeking the help of others - the victim let down by the system - to being a source of advice, of inspiration.
ANDY KAWA – WOMEN'S RIGHTS ACTIVIST
ANDY - I don't find it a burden. I find it part of my journey, and I think sometimes people want information. People want somebody to listen to them and so I embrace that.



PROMOS


PROMO 1

VO – An investigation so flawed that 12 years after the crime, no arrests have been made.
BUSHIE – I couldn't believe all the mistakes they made. It was a comedy of errors from the outset.
VO – A survivor exposes police inefficiencies.
ANDY - There was nothing else for me. The only thing I wanted, i wanted some semblance of justice.


PROMO 2


VO – A former police officer says it’s the worst investigation he’s seen after 43 years of service.
BUSHIE - There wasn't a proper search done in that area. They went in the wrong direction.
VO – Why Andy Kawa’s relentless quest for justice ended up at the Constitutional Court
ANDY - Up to this day, there has not been one person who has been arrested for the case.
PROMO 3
VO - A brutal attack, a bungled investigation and a twelve-year long search for justice – how Andy Kawa’s Constitutional Court victory could be a game changer for victims of crime.
